Hotspot: Oversized login background SVG replaced with lightweight image
Evidence: The login configuration now selects login-background_en.png (about 32 KB), and the DHA build no longer copies the 13 MB login-background_ksm.svg into the frontend.
Potential Impact: The change avoids transferring and parsing the 13 MB SVG on the login route, reducing first-paint latency, browser memory, CPU use, and bandwidth consumption.
Recommended Remediation: Verify the login page visually after the next DHA build and retain a production performance budget below 300 KB for the background image.

Hotspot: Prebuilt override directories contain large JavaScript and source-map payloads
Affected Area: dist-form-entry; dist-patient-chart; dist-patient-tests; dist-patient-orders; dist-patient-medications; dist-primary-navigation; dist-service-queues; dist-dispense-app
Evidence: The eight tracked dist directories total about 82 MB and 4,504 files; JavaScript is about 40.04 MiB and 2,116 source maps consume about 25.93 MiB.
Potential Impact: Deployments, archive creation, extraction, file scanning, backups, and cache invalidation take longer; serving maps publicly also wastes disk and can disclose source.
Recommended Remediation: Generate overrides in CI from pinned sources, publish only required production files, exclude .map files from production artifacts unless secured, and enforce bundle/file-count budgets.

Hotspot: Override copy routine may merge stale files into generated package directories
Evidence: Each script renames a tracked dist directory to the generated versioned package name and recursively copies it onto a package directory already created by the OpenMRS build; it does not first remove or validate the generated destination.
Potential Impact: Depending on cp behavior and differing chunk manifests, nested directories or obsolete hashed chunks can remain, enlarging releases and risking clients loading incompatible assets.
Recommended Remediation: Replace the destination atomically from a clean staging directory, fail on unexpected layouts, delete orphan chunks, and validate the final import map plus duplicate/nested directory counts.

Hotspot: Production build resolves a mutable login-app version
Evidence: The production module map specifies @kenyaemr/esm-login-app as latest while other modules are version pinned.
Potential Impact: Identical source revisions can produce different bundles and performance characteristics; an upstream release can unexpectedly increase payload or regress startup.
Recommended Remediation: Pin an exact tested login-app version and update it through a measured dependency-upgrade process with bundle-size comparisons.

Hotspot: Several build entry points use mutable CLI tags
Affected Area: dev-build.sh:14 and 22; ethipioa_build.sh:14 and 22; taifa_care_build.sh:14 and 22
Evidence: Development and Ethiopia builds invoke openmrs@next, while the Taifa Care build invokes openmrs@latest for both build and assemble.
Potential Impact: Build time, output chunking, runtime memory use, and caching can change without a repository change, making regressions hard to reproduce or bisect.
Recommended Remediation: Pin one exact CLI version per supported distribution, record it in the package lock, and update deliberately after performance smoke tests.

Hotspot: Frontend build is repeated independently across deployment workflows
Evidence: A push to main builds and uploads the frontend in the development workflow, which then dispatches other workflows; QA independently checks out and runs the build script again.
Potential Impact: The same dependency resolution and bundle assembly consume CI minutes multiple times and may produce non-identical outputs when mutable versions are involved.
Recommended Remediation: Build one immutable artifact once, attach checksums and environment-specific config separately, then promote the verified artifact to QA/HIE/production.

Hotspot: Large configuration overlays are loaded during application bootstrap
Evidence: The production shell loads two configuration URLs totaling about 35 KB; other environments load overlays as large as 47 KB, with substantial repeated module configuration.
Potential Impact: Bootstrap must download, parse, merge, and validate broad configuration even for routes that use only a subset; duplication increases parse/allocation cost and configuration drift.
Recommended Remediation: Remove obsolete/default-equivalent settings, share generated common configuration, minify production JSON, enable compression and long-lived caching with content hashes, and measure config merge time.

Hotspot: Several declarative forms are very large
Evidence: The largest form definitions are approximately 242 KB, 220 KB, and 158 KB, and the ampathforms directory contains about 6.3 MB of JSON.
Potential Impact: Opening a large form can cause noticeable JSON parsing, schema traversal, expression evaluation, DOM construction, and browser heap spikes on low-memory workstations.
Recommended Remediation: Profile the largest forms on target hardware; split clinically independent sections, lazy-render collapsed sections, remove duplicate metadata, and define form-load/render budgets.

Hotspot: Configuration package contains hundreds of metadata artifacts
Evidence: The repository has 285 JSON/XML/CSV configuration files plus OCL and metadata-sharing ZIPs; the Maven assembly packages the entire configuration directory.
Potential Impact: Initial installation and upgrade can spend substantial time parsing, validating, and matching metadata, with temporary JVM heap pressure proportional to artifact complexity.
Recommended Remediation: Measure initializer timing and peak heap on clean install and upgrade, retire superseded files, divide large imports into bounded sets where supported, and avoid re-importing unchanged artifacts.

Hotspot: Workflow archives the complete generated frontend with verbose file traversal
Evidence: Deployment creates a tar.gz from the full frontend directory and uploads it for each commit; the tracked overrides alone contain thousands of files and tens of MiB before compression.
Potential Impact: Archive creation/extraction, network transfer, and activation time grow with every retained chunk/map, extending deployments and increasing temporary disk usage.
Recommended Remediation: Prune the frontend before archiving, exclude maps and orphan chunks, use content-addressed artifacts/delta-aware delivery where practical, and publish compressed/uncompressed size metrics.

Hotspot: No module-owned Java runtime implementation exists
Affected Area: src/main; pom.xml:7-8; repository Java source count
Evidence: The repository contains zero .java files and the Maven project has pom packaging; src/main only defines the assembly descriptor.
Potential Impact: No Java stream, thread, scheduler, static collection, Hibernate session, or JDBC leak can originate from this repository's own runtime code. Runtime leaks may still exist in the modules and frontend packages selected by this configuration.
Recommended Remediation: Treat JVM leak analysis as not applicable here; profile the assembled distribution and audit each referenced backend module separately. For browser leaks, run route-navigation heap snapshots against the built frontend.
